Leonard took $11 million less than his maximum extension number — on top of waiving a $7.45 million kicker to accommodate his trade from the Clippers — as the sides discussed flexibility for the Raptors' rising salary books.

Both sides maintained consistent dialogue on Leonard’s long-term Raptors future since July after the reunion via trade — and the two-time Finals MVP expects to finish his career in Toronto. Leonard, 35, now has a total of three years and $165 million on his Raptors deal.

Kawhi Leonard is locking in his long-term future in Toronto 🔒

The two-time NBA Finals MVP agreed to a two-year, $115 million contract extension with the Raptors earlier, complete with a player option for the 2028-29 season.

The deal keeps Kawhi under contract in Canada for the next three years, cementing his return to the franchise he once led to a championship 🏆

When you break down his career earnings by franchise, Kawhi’s ability to secure the bag is absolutely staggering.

He made $63.9 million during his years with the Spurs.

He earned $291.7 million during his era with the Clippers.

And got about $20 million during his first championship stint with the Raptors.

Now, adding this new $115 million extension, his second run in Toronto is pushing his career financial numbers among the highest-paid players ever 💰

What makes this extension even more significant is the financial sacrifice Kawhi made to help the front office build.

Leonard took $11 million less than his maximum extension amount, on top of waiving a $7.45 million trade kicker to facilitate his deal from the Clippers.

By leaving money on the table, Kawhi gave Toronto the roster and cap flexibility needed to manage their rising salary books alongside their young core 🙌

This move delivers on what Shams Charania reported recently: that Kawhi views this second stint as a chance to finish his career in Toronto and retire as a Raptor.

Can Kawhi Leonard and the Raptors make another deep championship run together before he hangs them up? 🤔
